steps.label: 1: a state is a normalized vector in a Hilbert space
steps.sub: A single qubit: |ψ⟩ = a|0⟩ + b|1⟩, with |a|² + |b|² = 1

steps.label: That vector is the complete description
steps.sub: Nothing requires a hidden definite classical value underneath

steps.label: 2: observables are Hermitian operators
steps.sub: Position, energy, or which basis you measure in

steps.label: Hermitian guarantees real eigenvalues
steps.sub: A measured quantity must come out real, never complex

steps.label: 3: a measurement always returns an eigenvalue
steps.sub: Never anything in between, never outside that fixed list

steps.label: The Born rule gives the probability of each outcome
steps.sub: Probability equals the squared magnitude of the relevant amplitude

steps.label: 4: the state collapses to match the outcome
steps.sub: Immediately after measuring, the superposition is gone

steps.label: A repeat measurement now gives the same result
steps.sub: With certainty — there's nothing left to produce a different outcome

code:
|psi> = 0.6|0> + 0.8|1>

normalization: 0.6^2 + 0.8^2 = 1  (OK)

P(0) = 0.6^2 = 0.36
P(1) = 0.8^2 = 0.64
sum check: 0.36 + 0.64 = 1  (OK)

if outcome = 1 -> state collapses to |1>
caption: Amplitudes aren't probabilities — square their magnitude to get one, then the state collapses to match whatever you got.

steps.label: 5: a closed system evolves unitarily over time
steps.sub: Smooth, deterministic, and always reversible between measurements

steps.label: This is why every quantum gate is a unitary matrix
steps.sub: A gate is just a chunk of closed-system time evolution

steps.label: Postulate 1 is 'what a qubit's state is'
steps.sub: Postulate 5 is 'what a gate does to it'

steps.label: Postulates 2-4 are 'what happens when you read it out'
steps.sub: There is no sixth postulate hiding something extra underneath

subtitle: Drawing the line: what this course covers in full rigor, and what it deliberately skips.
